faq.answer: Chief resident scheduling is the process of building ACGME-compliant block, call, clinic, and attending schedules for a residency or fellowship program. It is difficult because it requires simultaneously satisfying dozens of overlapping rules (duty hour rules, rotation minimums, resident preferences, coverage requirements, and subspecialty-specific ACGME regulations) while being resolved in a short window of time by a clinician with no formal scheduling training.
faq.question: What is chief resident scheduling and why is it so difficult?

faq.answer: Our team builds in the ACGME duty hour rules at the moment the schedule is generated. This includes the 80-hour weekly limit, minimum rest requirements, the 24-hour hard cap, and subspecialty-specific rules relevant to your program. Compliance is built into the output, chiefs do not need to manually audit the schedule after the fact.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard handle ACGME duty hour compliance for chief residents?

faq.answer: No. Scheduling Wizard is a managed service, not self-service software. Chief residents submit their program's rules and receive finished schedules as ready-to-use Excel files. There is no platform to log into, no interface to learn, and no onboarding burden. The Excel outputs can be uploaded directly to existing publishing platform.
faq.question: Do chief residents need to learn new software to use Scheduling Wizard?

faq.answer: With traditional spreadsheet-based scheduling, institutional knowledge is lost every time chiefs rotate. Scheduling Wizard retains your program's rules, requests, and scheduling configuration year over year. When a new chief starts, they inherit a fully built, optimized system rather than beginning from a blank spreadsheet, eliminating the ramp-up burden that typically comes with each annual transition.
faq.question: What happens to scheduling knowledge when a new chief resident takes over?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard generates Block and rotation schedules, Call schedules with fairness optimization, Clinic schedules, and Attending schedules. All schedule types are optimized simultaneously using the same rule set, so a change in one schedule type automatically resolves dependencies across the others.
faq.question: What types of schedules does Scheduling Wizard generate for residency programs?

faq.answer: Yes. Subspecialty-specific ACGME rules are built into the schedule itself. This is the most common question asked during program evaluations, and it is a core design requirement of the service. Programs can also submit custom rules with Scheduling Wizard, including the ones unique to their site or program structure.
